$comment: C1 closed vocabularies and the channel model. See PRODUCT.md §9.2 and §9.4.

$grounding.source: Google Analytics 4 default channel group rules (support.google.com/analytics/answer/9756891), read 2026-09-15.
$grounding.weights: Channels are drawn by weight, not uniformly. A uniform draw across eleven channels is itself a tell: real traffic is dominated by organic search, social and email, and a population of visitors arriving evenly from SMS, push and display would stand out in any aggregate channel report. The weights below are a plausible mix, not a measurement — they are deliberately coarse, and they are checked by test/coherence/run.mjs only for gross deviation.
$grounding.why: A fabricated persona has to land in a NAMED channel. GA4 assigns any source/medium pair its rules do not recognize to 'Unassigned', and an Unassigned row is the first thing an analyst filters out — so an incoherent persona is not merely implausible, it is discarded before anyone looks at it. Every channel below is therefore modelled on a real GA4 channel group, and test/ga4-channels.mjs re-implements those rules as an oracle so the property is checked rather than asserted.

excluded.Affiliates: GA4 assigns medium 'affiliate' to the Affiliates channel. Never emitted: PRODUCT.md §11.1 constraint 1 forbids fabricating affiliate attribution.
excluded.Paid Shopping / Organic Shopping: Both key off shopping-campaign patterns tied to commercial outcomes. Out of scope for the same reason.
excluded.Direct: Source '(direct)' with medium '(none)' is the absence of attribution, which is what stripping already produces. Nothing to fabricate.

email.$rule: Source or medium matches email|e-mail|e_mail|e mail.

organic_social.$rule: Source in GA4's social sites list OR medium in (social, social-network, social-media, sm).

paid_social.$rule: Source in GA4's social sites list AND medium matches ^(.*cp.*|ppc|retargeting|paid.*)$. Sources here are restricted to platforms on that list — a source GA4 does not recognise as social would fall through to Paid Other.

organic_search.$rule: Source in GA4's search sites list OR medium exactly 'organic'.

paid_search.$rule: Source in GA4's search sites list AND medium matches ^(.*cp.*|ppc|retargeting|paid.*)$.

display.$rule: Medium in (display, banner, expandable, interstitial, cpm).

organic_video.$rule: Source in GA4's video sites list OR medium matches .*video.*

push.$rule: Medium ends with 'push', or contains 'notification' or 'mobile'; or source is exactly 'firebase'.

utm_term.$note: The paid keyword field. Emitting it outside a paid channel is a tell, so the engine omits it unless the incoming URL carried it — and if it did, the channel is already constrained toward paid.

$refWarning: ref and source are also common affiliate fields. Values matching the commerce group in never-touch.json suppress substitution for the whole URL before any of this is consulted.
